_meta.source: Reverse-engineered: USB MIDI capture of Axe-Edit III traffic + accessibility-driven parameter sweeps. ids are firmware-internal enums.
_meta.warning: param ids, model ids, and scales are specific to FW 32.02; a firmware update could renumber them. Re-capture to verify on other firmware.

protocol.set_param: F0 00 01 74 10 01 09 00 <blk_lo blk_hi> <pid_lo pid_hi> <v0 v1 v2 v3 v4> 00 00 00 00 <cks> F7
protocol.ids: block id and param id are 14-bit: lo | (hi<<7)
protocol.value_encoding: value = displayed_value / scale, encoded as IEEE-754 float32 little-endian, packed as 5 x 7-bit MIDI septets (LSB first)
protocol.checksum: XOR of all bytes from F0 through the last data byte, & 0x7F

scales.null: nonlinear display (e.g. capacitance) -> store/send the raw float directly

protocol.transport: Send to 'Axe-Fx III MIDI Out'. Works with Axe-Edit open. In mido, sysex data = frame without F0/F7.
protocol.example: set AMP1 Gain to 7.5: param_id=1, scale=10 -> float 0.75
protocol.alt_set_param_0152: RESOLVED 2026-06-24 PM-2: func 0x01 sub 0x52 is a FIXED alt-SET opcode (NOT block-encoded). Frame layout identical to 01 09 with the sub byte = 0x52. DEVICE-VERIFIED on 3 independent blocks: Flanger Bass Focus (block 0x52, pid 26), Delay Drive (block 0x46, pid 16, scale 10), Cab Drive (block 0x3E, pid 33, scale 10) -- the latter two have block ids != 0x52, which disambiguates (the Flanger 0x52==0x52 was a coincidence). For all of these, plain 01 09 to the SAME numeric pid does NOT set the param (it is unreachable via 01 09 -- a different param namespace). The firmware-added 'Drive' param is an alt-SET class: Delay & Cab Drive verified; Chorus(0x4E pid20), Flanger(0x52 pid20), Rotary(0x56 pid17), Wah(0x5E pid10), DynaDist(0xCA pid7) are pattern-inferred alt-SET (unverified). BUILDER CAVEAT: set_parameter/build_preset emit 01 09 and will silently no-op for these params -- honor the param's set_command='01 52'. Method to find more: direct_probe_map a block, the sliders that 01 09 cannot move are alt-SET candidates; confirm by capturing Axe-Edit's TX (capture_altset.py). UPDATE PM-2: the alt-SET class is BROADER than 'Drive' -- IR Player (0xC3) Low Cut (pid 2) and High Cut (pid 3) are also alt-SET (01 09 no-op, 01 52 works). So 0x52 = the SET command for a set of firmware-added params of any kind, not just Drive.

duplicate_listing.why: CAB pid 8 `Level` is listed twice: here and in the other container named below. The fields are identical, so this is a plain re-listing, NOT a BUG-19 shared-pid pair (a shared-pid pair is two DIFFERENT names for one storage, e.g. DELAY pid 4 as `Feedback` and `Feedback L>L`, where deleting either loses a way to address the pid). Neither copy was removed, on three grounds: `dynacab.params` is GENERATED wholesale by build_master_map.py from the CABDYNA block map, so a deletion here desynchronises the map from its generator and is undone by the next rebuild; pid 8 is not special -- 21 of the 46 dynacab entries are field-identical to a main-list row and 22 more re-list the same pid under a DIFFERENT name or scale, so removing the one tidy case fixes nothing while making the shadow list look handled; and pids [76, 80, 101] exist ONLY in the dynacab list, so it is not a subset that could simply be dropped. SEPARATE AND LARGER: axefx_core._block_all_params synthesizes a THIRD route to this pid, `Level 1`, from dynacab.mics[0]['level'], carrying scale 1.0 where both map rows say 0.001 -- three spellings of one hazard-4 pid that disagree on scale. Harmless on the write path today because the probed domain is `display`, under which scale is ignored, but any consumer reporting `scale` gets a different answer per spelling. That is a scale audit, not a de-dupe, and it was not made here.

words_per_channel_evidence.confidence_downgrade_reason: S54 fold 2026-07-25: DOWNGRADED from the inference-returned 'high'. The 42 words are six IDENTICAL 7-word rows ([0, 0, 52427, 32767, 0, 0, 0] x6), so periods 7, 14 and 21 all fit. The 2 x 21 split scored 'high' only because the two 21-word halves match -- and they match because the ROW repeats, which is not evidence of a channel split. If MUX is really one channel of 42 laid out as six rows, this bound of 21 is too LOW, which is the dangerous direction: a too-low bound turns real mapped pids into false map errors. The bound is left at the measured value; only the confidence was overstated, and 'low' makes it WARN rather than enforce on writes (ADDRESS_BOUND_ENFORCING_CONFIDENCES). Do not enforce against MUX pids above 20 on the strength of this.

CONTROL.note: S28 device (2026-07-10 daytime, E15 F15.1 discovery spike -- the CONTROLLERS surface CRACKED; extends S26/S27): SYSTEM block, official enum ID_CONTROL = 2 -- NOT a grid effect block (not placeable/bypassable; no instances). +120 params added S28 via the Axe-Edit Controllers view + broadcast/announce catch: LFO 1/2, ADSR 1/2, Envelope, Sequencer + 32 stages, Manual 1-5, Scene Ctrl 1-4, Pitch Input Source -- every entry caught live, stepped once, inverse-restored; final census diff 0 (_drafts_s28/_s28_ctl_census_final2.json vs _s28_ctl_census.json). *** DEVICE-PERSISTENT LAW (S28): CONTROL block writes PERSIST across preset changes (PC 1 -> PC 0 twice) AND Axe-Edit close -- NOT preset-scoped edit-buffer state. Treat exactly like GLOBAL: autosave-like, NO reload-to-revert; the only restore is writing the old value back (read/record BEFORE any write). *** ANNOUNCE LAWS (S28): combos/enums announce via the S27 broadcast law (unsolicited 01 09, value = idx/(N-1)); continuous params (sliders) do NOT emit 01 09 -- they announce via the 01 0C / 01 0D sub family (and 01 0A / 01 0B for some, e.g. Quantize/Stages): 60-byte frames, SAME field layout as 09 (blk d[8..9], pid d[10..11], value septets d[12:17], normalized value); empirically 0C/0A fire on the step (new value), 0D/0B on the inverse/commit -- decode all four like 09 (a slider walk that only listens for 09 sees nothing). Other ambient subs catalogued: 01 56 on Controllers-view open (view/target-select suspect); 01 22/01 23 = request/bulk-dump pair (0x23 = 609 B, block 2 pid 2) on page nav; 01 39 23-B echo frames; 01 01 (87 B, block 0x25) ambient. *** MODIFIER GET (S28, CORRECTED S30): sub 01 07 reads ZERO even with a modifier attached -- it is NOT the modifier-slot read channel. S30 (device-verified FW 32.02) proved 01 07 stays all-zero across selectors 0-15 both before AND after a real modifier was attached; the REAL modifier-slot read is fn 0x1F on slot blocks 3-26 (25-word field table: w0 Source1, w8 target blk, w9 target prm, ... see PROTOCOL_ADDITIONS_S30.md). The 01 07 frame (F0 00 01 74 10 01 07 00 <blk14> <pid14> <sel> 00 <cks> F7 -> 23-byte 01 19-shaped reply, selector not echoed) records as not-the-answer. Top-level II-style func 0x07 NAKs 64 07 05. *** MODIFIER ATTACH/DETACH (S30, F15.3 CLOSED, no USBPcap): ATTACH = 01 3a with target blk/prm (unit echoes 23-B 01 3a + assigns a slot 3-26); read slots via 0x1F; source SET = index-as-float via 01 09 on slot prm0; DETACH = 01 09 slot prm0=0.0 then 01 3b <slot14>. Full frames + 25-field map + 75-source enum in PROTOCOL_ADDITIONS_S30.md. *** S29 (2026-07-10 evening, E15 tails -- census diff 0 after every script, statusdump == baseline 9): LFO 1/2 Type enum WALKED = 10 entries {Sine .. Astable} (see pids 0/6; UI combo list alphabetical and WRAPS); Scene Ctrl 3 (88-95) / 4 (96-103) upgraded stride-inferred -> device-verified (paired 'Scene Ctrl 3+4' page walk, scenes 1/8 of each bank announced exactly the inferred pids); pids 171-174 dispositioned READ-ONLY (write-deaf via 01 09; GETs 1.0/-1.0/1.0/-1.0; hypothesis = ADSR 1/2 X/Y display-mark coordinates per the AxeBlockEdit import brief, symbol table with ~3-pid drift -- confirm via static oracle, not device probing). *** DO-NOT-WRITE (S29 hot zone): CONTROL pids 178-188 = *_SET_ALL action pids per the AxeBlockEdit brief -- NEVER probe-write above pid 174 until the drift is anchored. *** Tempo history (S26/S27, still true): preset tempo = pid 32 (SET = 01 09 raw BPM float), Tempo To Use = pid 33 {Preset,Global}; func 0x14 is GET-only and returns the STORED (flash) preset tempo (stale -- useless as a live reader); the GLOBAL tempo lives at GLOBAL (id 1) pid 0. They are there. The mapping work they represent is ONE table decoder, not 48 param rows: do not open 48 gap rows for them, and do not let a future census count them as 48 unmapped pids. The same dump also bounds this block: 712 words that split into four BYTE-IDENTICAL 178-word channel slices, i.e. 178 addresses per channel (= max mapped pid 177 + 1), so any CONTROL pid >= 178 is a map error. CONTROL.set_domain_audit_s53: SET-DOMAIN AUDIT, 2026-07-25 (S53, OFFLINE -- no device) (BUG-32 family sweep). Every string in this map was searched for a SET-domain claim ('raw display percent', 'raw percent', 'SET = raw', 'SET is the', 'x100 family', 'display percent' and near variants). 317 params across 6 blocks make one; the rest carry no SET-domain prose at all. Per-param risk markers were added as `set_domain_caution` on 112 pids -- all of them CONTINUOUS-value pids, where a domain error produces a wrong MAGNITUDE. The remaining 182 are ENUM/INDEX SETs (151 of them carrying explicit device attestation) ('SET = 01 09 float(idx)' / 'raw index': CONTROL 0-177, CONTROLSWITCHES 1285+, FCLAYOUT, CAB 85-92, the GLOBAL External-Control sources 1302-1313 and the MIDI-bypass-CC table 192-340). Those are NOT individually flagged: the combo law is protocol-wide and independently attested (CLAUDE.md, amp pid 0 = float(model_id)), most carry S27 SET-and-watch or S49 set+revert attribution, and a wrong enum picks a wrong mode rather than a wrong level. TWO enum exceptions worth knowing anyway: GLOBAL 56/57 (Output 1/2 Level, {+4 dBu:0, -10 dBV:1}) -- a one-index slip is an ~11.8 dB output-reference jump, the loudest single-value mistake available in this block; and GLOBAL 58/59 (Input 3/4 Boost/Pad), whose 12 dB / 18 dB labels are family-inferred and marked '?' in the source findings. STRUCTURAL FINDING, HANDED BACK: this map has no `set_domain` field, so the SET domain is encoded implicitly by `scale` (axefx_core._coerce_param_value sends float(value)/scale). Wherever the prose and `scale` disagree, THE WRITE PATH FOLLOWS `scale` and the prose is decoration -- which is why correcting BUG-32's note on 44-47 did not stop the write path reproducing it. Two regions inside that space are STORAGE, not parameters, and a future census must NOT chase them as unmapped pids: *** (1) words 678-772 are a PRINTABLE-CHARACTER TABLE *** (a contiguous run of printable-ASCII words, found by text_runs() -- the same pass that recovers the FC layout names 'Layout 1'..'Layout 8' and 'MstrLayout'); *** (2) words from ~8470 upward are a SONG-NAME LIST *** ('Song 001', 'Song 002', ...). GLOBAL.set_domain_audit_s53: SET-DOMAIN AUDIT, 2026-07-25 (S53, OFFLINE -- no device) (BUG-32 family sweep). Every string in this map was searched for a SET-domain claim ('raw display percent', 'raw percent', 'SET = raw', 'SET is the', 'x100 family', 'display percent' and near variants). 317 params across 6 blocks make one; the rest carry no SET-domain prose at all. Per-param risk markers were added as `set_domain_caution` on 112 pids -- all of them CONTINUOUS-value pids, where a domain error produces a wrong MAGNITUDE. The remaining 182 are ENUM/INDEX SETs (151 of them carrying explicit device attestation) ('SET = 01 09 float(idx)' / 'raw index': CONTROL 0-177, CONTROLSWITCHES 1285+, FCLAYOUT, CAB 85-92, the GLOBAL External-Control sources 1302-1313 and the MIDI-bypass-CC table 192-340). Those are NOT individually flagged: the combo law is protocol-wide and independently attested (CLAUDE.md, amp pid 0 = float(model_id)), most carry S27 SET-and-watch or S49 set+revert attribution, and a wrong enum picks a wrong mode rather than a wrong level. TWO enum exceptions worth knowing anyway: GLOBAL 56/57 (Output 1/2 Level, {+4 dBu:0, -10 dBV:1}) -- a one-index slip is an ~11.8 dB output-reference jump, the loudest single-value mistake available in this block; and GLOBAL 58/59 (Input 3/4 Boost/Pad), whose 12 dB / 18 dB labels are family-inferred and marked '?' in the source findings. STRUCTURAL FINDING, HANDED BACK: this map has no `set_domain` field, so the SET domain is encoded implicitly by `scale` (axefx_core._coerce_param_value sends float(value)/scale). Wherever the prose and `scale` disagree, THE WRITE PATH FOLLOWS `scale` and the prose is decoration -- which is why correcting BUG-32's note on 44-47 did not stop the write path reproducing it. Report: _s53_setdomain_risk_report.md. See E17 F17.2.
